title: New York City microhubs convert truck delivery into smaller last-mile operation
source_unit: New York City Department of Transportation Microhubs Pilot
geography: New York City, Manhattan, United States

truck_trips_replaced.unit: truck trips; more than this number in the first year

new_microhub_locations_announced.unit: locations; Financial District and Upper East Side

observations.method: Transcribed from the NYC DOT official first-year Microhubs Pilot release. The record keeps the agency's reported counts and daily operating volumes separate from independent causal or neighborhood-level effects.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not provide a truck-trip denominator for the affected corridors, package-delivery quality, worker time or pay, recipient-level exposure, neighborhood noise or safety measurements, operating cost, or durable continuation after the pilot period.
observations.subgroup: Deliveries routed through NYC DOT microhubs on Manhattan's Upper West Side, Upper East Side, and Financial District; the release identifies delivery partners and locations but not all participating firms or recipients.
observations.counterinterpretation: Replacing truck trips with handcarts or cargo bikes can reduce truck exposure while shifting labor, curb-space, time, or delivery constraints to other actors; the reported pilot totals do not establish equal benefit or durable acceptance.

related_sources.claim: NYC DOT's congestion-pricing mitigation program separately funds off-hour delivery incentives; that route remains an announced mitigation program rather than a completed participant-level outcome.

boundary: This record establishes named microhub operation, alternative delivery modes, and agency-reported truck-mile and pollution reductions. It does not establish recipient-level service quality, worker or neighborhood incidence, cost savings, causal safety or air-quality effects, or durable public acceptance.
